Metadata.title: Dominik Huber – Full-Stack Developer
Metadata.description: Self-taught software developer from Germany, building fast, precise interfaces with Next.js, React and TypeScript.

HomePage.bio:
Hi 👋 I'm Dominik, a former automotive and engine engineering student at the <uni>University of Stuttgart</uni>. During the pandemic I taught myself programming, and I've been building software ever since, with a focus on interfaces that feel fast, precise and calm.

It started with <extensions>browser extensions</extensions> in plain <js>JavaScript</js>, and honestly a lot of wrestling with HTML and CSS, with great support from my team along the way. From there I moved into data: scraping pipelines in <python>Python</python> and <node>Node.js</node>. Eventually I found where I'm happiest: the frontend. Today I build with <next>Next.js</next>, <react>React</react> and <ts>TypeScript</ts>, and I care about the details you only notice when they're missing: type-safe APIs, accessible components, motion that supports instead of distracts, and interfaces that stay responsive under real data.
HomePage.bioAfterGraph: That foundation led me to build <profitpath>ProfitPath</profitpath>, an Amazon arbitrage platform that makes online arbitrage accessible for sellers. It processes data from 1,000+ companies and suppliers and 200M+ products updated daily, and turns it into tools like supplier search, wholesale scanning, competitor analysis and automated profit calculations. The hard part isn't the data, it's the UX: making millions of rows scannable, filterable and actionable in seconds. Want to know more? Reach out on <linkedin>LinkedIn</linkedin>

AboutPage.origin: I was born in Ulm, Germany, and I'm a passionate full-stack developer.

story.p1: I probably spend more time in front of a screen than I'd like to admit – but at least it's usually for a good reason. I love writing code, turning new ideas into something real and building, step by step, a thought into something that actually works in the end. Most of the time, anyway.
story.p2: My interest in technology goes far beyond programming, though. <apple>Apple</apple> in particular has won me over. I love good design, well-thought-out products and those small details that probably only delight people who spend far too long staring at user interfaces. So I usually follow new Apple products with a mix of excitement and the question of whether I really need them. We both probably know the answer.
story.p3: When I need a break from the screen, you'll often find me on the <golf>golf course</golf>. I like the mix of calm, focus and the fact that this sport regularly reminds you not to take yourself too seriously. Some days everything goes exactly as planned – and on others you're just happy to find your ball again.
story.p4: A completely different side of me is my passion for <latam>Latin America</latam>. I love the music, the culture, the joy of life and especially the energy that comes with it. Latin music is on pretty much all the time – whether I'm working, on the go, or when “just one song” has suddenly turned into an entire playlist.
story.p5: In the end, I'm probably a somewhat unusual mix: developer, Apple enthusiast, golfer and big fan of Latin American culture.
story.p6: And that mix actually describes me pretty well.

LocationsPage.title: Locations
LocationsPage.intro:
Originally, I'm from the south of Germany – Ulm, to be precise. After 26 years, I took the leap and started over in a new city: Cologne, in the <heart>heart</heart> of NRW, Germany. Today, NRW is still my home.

The fastest way to get in touch is to send me a simple <email>email</email>. I should reply within a few hours. Got a project in mind that would be a good fit? Then book a 15-minute call with me directly on <cal>Cal.com</cal>

TechStackPage.title: Tech stack
TechStackPage.description: The tools and technologies Dominik Huber works with: Next.js, React, TypeScript and more.
TechStackPage.intro: The tools I work with and the projects they're part of. It started with browser extensions in plain JavaScript; today it's platforms like ProfitPath, built with Next.js and TypeScript. Here you can see how well I know each tool and where I've used it.

nextjs.name: Next.js
nextjs.description: Server rendering, static pages, routing, data fetching and image optimization in one. ProfitPath is built on it, and so is this site.

react.name: React
react.description: The library for interfaces, in almost everything I build: web apps, extensions and, with React Native, mobile apps too.

reactNative.name: React Native & Expo
reactNative.description: We built the NexosSolutions app for Android and iOS with it, from one codebase for both platforms.

chromeExtensions.name: Chrome extensions & Webpack
chromeExtensions.description: Extensions built with React and bundled with Webpack: automated purchasing software, scrapers and small helpers that work where you already are.

typescript.name: TypeScript
typescript.description: Part of almost all my projects. Types make interfaces unambiguous, and many bugs show up while writing instead of in front of users.

javascript.name: JavaScript
javascript.description: NexosSolutions was a browser extension in plain JavaScript that automated selecting, buying and ordering limited items through web requests.

python.name: Python
python.description: A university in Munich hired me for a project that collects data from the web for research and teaching.

go.name: Go
go.description: Extremely fast and efficient. In some projects a Go backend delivered the data to the frontend and handled the API requests.

nodejs.name: Node.js & Express
nodejs.description: The backend behind NexosSolutions: the API that supplied the extension and the app with data.

orpc.name: oRPC
orpc.description: Makes type-safe APIs almost effortless and fits right in with Next.js Server Actions and TanStack Query, which is why we use it in our projects.

tanstack.name: TanStack
tanstack.description: Developer experience first: Query fetches the data, Table shows it in ProfitPath's large tables. This site uses TanStack Query as well.

postgresql.name: PostgreSQL
postgresql.description: An open-source database with over 30 years of development, known for its reliability, feature set and performance.

mongodb.name: MongoDB
mongodb.description: NoSQL with JSON-like documents. At NexosSolutions it held the user and product data of the extension and the app.

supabase.name: Supabase
supabase.description: An open-source platform built on PostgreSQL. At ProfitPath, Supabase runs sign-in and keeps subscriptions in sync.

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.description: At ProfitPath, Stripe handles the payments and enables flexible payment options.

betterAuth.name: Better Auth
betterAuth.description: Probably the most comprehensive open-source authentication system for web apps.

profitpath.title: ProfitPath
profitpath.description: A platform for Amazon sellers. Finds profitable products for online arbitrage: supplier search, wholesale scanning, competitor analysis and automatic profit calculation, updated daily from the data of over 1,000 companies and suppliers.

profitgo.title: ProfitGo
profitgo.description: Product analysis on the go. The second product of the ProfitPath family: analyze products as soon as you visit a website or scan a barcode.

nexossolutions.title: NexosSolutions
nexossolutions.description: Automated purchasing software. A browser extension in plain JavaScript, HTML and CSS, plus an app for Android and iOS and its own API with a database behind it.

nexosproxies.title: NexosProxies
nexosproxies.description: A proxy network as a service. My own IP proxy network, first to cut my own costs, then as a service for others in the same situation.

portfolio.title: huberdominik.com
portfolio.description: My portfolio, the site you're on right now: bilingual without language URLs, text that streams in, a map with a driving car and a navigation written as a sentence.
